description: This bar chart illustrates the number of datasets categorized by year, specifically differentiating between datasets labeled “1+” and “2+”. The horizontal axis represents “Year”, with labels ranging from 2012 to 2022, appearing in chronological order. The vertical axis is labeled “Number of datasets” and represents a linear scale ranging from 0 to 100, with tick marks at 20-unit intervals. Two bars are present for each year, grouped side-by-side; the blue bars represent datasets labeled “1+”, and the orange bars represent datasets labeled “2+”. In 2012, both the “1+” and “2+” bars are minimal, reaching approximately 1 and 0.5 datasets respectively. The “1+” bars generally increase in height over time, reaching a maximum of approximately 104 datasets in 2021, while the “2+” bars also increase, peaking at around 48 datasets in 2021. The shortest “1+” bar is in 2013, at approximately 2 datasets, and the shortest “2+” bar is in 2012, at approximately 0.5 datasets. No bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, outlining, or annotations.
